title: Pair-primitive quaternary local-global deduction: imported analytic source

source.author: Jeremy Rouse
source.title: Integers represented by positive-definite quadratic forms and Petersson inner products
statements_used: Equation (1), PDF page 5: genus coefficient as product of local densities.
Theorem 3, PDF page 10: polynomial bound for Petersson norm of cuspidal part.
Start of Section 5, PDF page 15, combined PDF page 16: general all-n coefficient bound; no coprimality assumption on n.
source.inspection_scope: Actual v1 PDF statements and their combination inspected internally; imported proofs have not been independently reconstructed.
source.normalization_note: The real factor 4*pi^2*n/sqrt(det Gram) is derived independently from ellipsoid volume. The displayed pi^2 prefactor in Rouse Section 3 has an apparent factor-of-four discrepancy with its stated Gram convention; it is not copied.

limitations: Priority for the two-block deduction unaudited.
Finite checker challenges normalizations and selected cases; it does not establish analytic uniformity.
No numerical cutoff is supplied for the general binary-pair theorem; the separate -8 sieve supplies 2^78 and complete prime coverage. Exact -8/-11 binary exception lists remain unresolved.
Coordinate counts are not unweighted value-pair asymptotics.

dyadic_sources.author: Jacob Sturm
dyadic_sources.title: On the Congruence of Modular Forms
dyadic_sources.version: Lecture Notes in Mathematics 1240 (1987), 275–280; retained official two-page preview pp.275–276
statements_used: Theorem 1, printed p.276: equality modulo a prime follows when the difference has order greater than k times the group index divided by 12.
Applied modulo every rational prime to integer coefficient forms, this proves equality from coefficients through floor(k times index divided by 12).
dyadic_sources.inspection_scope: Actual theorem statement and beginning of proof inspected in primary preview; the rest of the article is not retained or claimed inspected.

dyadic_scope: Exact unrestricted formulas (29)–(30) count only coordinate primitivity at 2 for Q=x^2+2y^2; odd inert prime obstructions are not removed. The q^0 through q^2 and q^0 through q^8 Sturm certificates establish their completeness under the sourced modularity statements.

minus8_spectral_dependency.scope: Proof of the finite quaternion quotient spectral lemma, including the exact all-ideal correspondence, norm characters, Jacquet-Langlands transfer and weight-two prime-power bounds.
minus8_spectral_dependency.specialization: Analytic note (32)–(36) verifies the replacement order, class-number-one double coset, unit normalization 4, local level at 2 and the finite 2-power operators; the cited external theorem editions are those pinned by this existing proof.

minus8_effective_scope.global_statement: Every N at least 2^78 with 16 not dividing N is a sum of two positive primitive -8 norm values.
minus8_effective_scope.all_prime_statement: Every prime N at least 2 belongs to P_-8+P_-8; analytic threshold 2^22 plus exhaustive retained finite certificate.
minus8_effective_scope.remaining_exact_classification: Equivalent to all N=2^e*m>=2, 0<=e<=3, odd m<2^60 with only primes 5 or 7 modulo 8; that finite family remains unchecked in full.
minus8_effective_scope.priority: The dyadic identities and finite-quotient method are classical; no priority claim for these explicit specializations.
minus8_effective_scope.distinct_value_lower_bound: At least N^(2/3)/4800 ordered value pairs for every N>=2^78 with16 not dividing N.
